title: Convex hull batched support without margin
summary: Recovered VA 0x47d0c0, 249 bytes, as a genuine thiscall member with the original partial hull layout. Iterates scaled vertices in source order, initializes only output w to exact -1e18f, computes (dx*x + dy*y) + dz*z in single precision, and replaces xyz and w only for an ordered strict improvement. Direct Game.exe disassembly and vtable 0x9fb128 slot +0x40 establish ABI and layout; caller 0x4644e4 passes direction, output, and count. The accepted oracle's complete 249 bytes were checked against Game.exe. Source is behavioral recovery, with no matching-code claim.
test_description: Freestanding GCC i386 oracle harness passed 460 differential cases: hull counts -1/0/1/2/12, direction counts -3/0/1/5/10, random finite vectors, nonuniform negative scaling, zero direction ties, quiet NaNs, infinities, sentinel-equal scores, signed zero and subnormal scaling, exact direction/output aliasing, and all four rounding modes on additional random cases. Compares every output byte including guards and untouched xyz, complete hull storage, vertex and direction arrays, and MXCSR including exception status. Known outputs independently assert empty-hull sentinel and zero-direction first winner. Uses original thiscall reference at its original VA; no dependencies or fixed data fixtures required. Local VS2013 Update 5 implementation compilation also checked.
known_limits: Only the assigned method is recovered; other virtual methods, allocation, hull construction and margin handling remain outside scope. Unused base/layout bytes have no inferred semantics.

Tests use valid allocated buffers, masked floating-point exceptions, and normal single-threaded execution. Invalid pointers, huge overflowing counts, asynchronous mutation, and Windows exception dispatch are not validated.
Exact direction/output aliasing is tested; partial overlaps and output aliasing the hull or vertex storage are not validated.

The x86 ordered comparison helper preserves COMISS status behavior. The non-x86 fallback preserves ordered comparison results but makes no claim about x86 exception flags. Floating-point contraction and fast-math must remain disabled.
No byte-match credit is claimed. Native Windows execution and compiler-generated byte parity are not established by the local MSVC compilation.
